standard_prerequisites.name: Uniqueness of isomorphisms of solutions
standard_prerequisites.use: Two solutions of a system with vanishing negative exts are uniquely isomorphic.

standard_prerequisites.name: Filtered colimits are exact
standard_prerequisites.use: Stalk computation of the colimit complex.

core_obligations: Transfinite construction of maps of complexes τ_{β,α} : (j_{β,α})_!I_β^• → I_α^• representing the adjoints of the inverses of ρ^α_β and satisfying τ_{γ,α} = τ_{β,α} ∘ (j_{β,α})_!τ_{γ,β}: successor case by the K-injectivity of I_α^• (proof lines 11363-11386).

Limit case: the termwise colimit C^• = colim_{β<α}(j_{β,α})_!I_β^• represents K_α — the coprojections restrict to quasi-isomorphisms σ_β : I_β^• → C^•|_{W_β} by the stalk computation using commutation of stalks with colimits, exactness of filtered colimits and the quasi-isomorphisms (I_β^•)_x → (I_{β'}^•)_x; then (C^•, σ_β^{-1}) and (K_α, ρ^α_β) are two solutions, giving a unique isomorphism σ by the solution-in-finite-case lemma (vanishing of negative exts), and τ_{β,α} = τ|_{W_β} ∘ σ_β (proof lines 11387-11417).

Define K as the object represented by K^• = colim_{α∈E}(W_α → X)_!I_α^• with transition maps τ_{β,α}; arguing exactly as above, the coprojection restrictions give isomorphisms K|_{W_α} → K_α compatible with the ρ^α_β (proof lines 11418-11452).
proof_roadmap: Construct compatible τ_{β,α} by transfinite recursion.
Handle limit ordinals with the colimit complex and solution uniqueness.
Take the final colimit and verify the restrictions.
difficulty_reason: A transfinite recursion constructs compatible maps of complexes τ_{β,α}; the limit-ordinal step uses a termwise colimit complex with a stalk-level quasi-isomorphism argument, and uniqueness of isomorphisms between solutions (using vanishing of negative exts); the final object is a colimit over E.
